title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false-positive failure of an automated licence plate reader, and it happened at the point where a machine-generated alert was passed to officers as a fact. The camera flagged a plate as stolen, and the stop, the drawn guns and the K-9 deployment all followed from that alert. The alert was wrong, and police learned this only afterwards. The failure is not that the system produced an error, it is that the error was consumed as a verified hit rather than as a lead.

The mismatch was present in the record before anyone was stopped. The camera image was linked to a Chevy Malibu, and the alert landed on a red Dodge Ram pickup. A human check comparing the flagged vehicle against the vehicle description attached to the alert would have caught it at the dispatch stage, before officers approached the truck. The K-9 policy described in the reporting requires handlers to weigh the severity of the crime, immediate threats, and whether a suspect is resisting or evading, and those judgements were being made on a stop that should not have happened.

What is not established is whether the misread was a technical fault or a handling error, and the reporting does not show intent by anyone involved. A department investigation found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, charges against the driver were later dropped, and the reports do not say what disciplinary or other steps followed.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Body camera video was released Monday showing Toledo police officers using a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, was stopped after a FLOCK camera alert about a stolen plate. Police later learned the alert was wrong. The camera image was linked to a Chevy Malibu but appeared on a red Dodge Ram pickup. Officers stopped the truck, drew guns, and repeatedly told Upchurch to get out. He exited with his hands up, then walked in the grass as the K-9 handler moved closer. He was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction. He received medical attention at the scene.

Police said they thought Upchurch might flee and did not know if he or a passenger had weapons. The article says multiple Toledo Police Department officers are under investigation. It does not say what disciplinary action or other next steps will follow. The report also notes TPD's K-9 policy requires handlers to consider the crime's severity, immediate threats, and whether a suspect is resisting or trying to evade arrest before deploying a dog.
